t: You can close this wound. Please do it before the fever starts.
Give the healer steady hands and give me enough sense to obey.
I know you see this pain. Help me endure what remains.
Mend what is torn and let me return to useful work.
If you can help this heal, I would be grateful.
The healer has done their part. Perhaps you could help with the rest.
I do not know whether pain reaches you. Mine is loud enough.
I trust the bandage more than prayer, but I am using both.
If you want belief, healing this would make a strong argument.
The healer says rest. I suppose asking you cannot hurt more.
Lead the builders to us. We need walls before the cold worsens.
You have given others shelter. Please remember us now.
Keep us warm tonight while hands prepare a proper roof.
I will help build it. Please help us reach that morning.
If you hear people without roofs, we are still here.
A dry night would feel enough like an answer.
I am asking for shelter, not certainty. Please send one of them.
Builders make roofs. If you exist, help them finish ours.
I have asked every person who might help. You are the last attempt.
A roof would persuade me more than another sermon about patience.
Hold the roofs down and keep the walls standing.
Turn the worst wind aside before it reaches the houses.
Guard everyone outside and guide them home through the rain.
You rule the sky. Show mercy to the people beneath it.
If storms listen to anybody, let this one listen to you.
The wind is rising. I hope you are nearer than it sounds.
Help the roofs hold, and I will decide what that means later.
Weather does not bargain, but perhaps you do. Spare the houses.
I expect the builders deserve more thanks. Help them anyway.
If you made this storm, stopping it would be a decent start.
Guide my steps and let the road end somewhere safe.
Watch the people travelling beyond our fires tonight.
Keep wolves away and bring every traveler home again.
Make the way plain when the path divides.
I do not know where this road leads. Perhaps you do.
If you travel with anyone, walk beside us for a while.
Help me choose the path I will regret least.
I trust my feet, but another pair of eyes would help.
If you know the shorter road, now is the time to mention it.
I am lost enough to ask anyone, including you.
Keep the wolves beyond the paths where our children walk.
Strengthen the guards and turn the pack toward empty ground.
Do not let another family hear wolves outside their door.
You know every creature. Keep these ones away from us.
Maybe wolves fear you. I know they do not fear me.
I heard them near the trees. Please let that be the closest they come.
Help the guards find the pack before the pack finds anyone alone.
Wolves understand spears better than prayers. Send people with spears.
If you protect this village, the howling is your chance to prove it.
I would prefer a strong fence, but I will ask you too.
Keep watch while the village sleeps and the fires burn low.
Stand beside the guards where their torches cannot reach.
Let every sleeper wake safely when morning comes.
Quiet the fears that grow larger after dark.
Night makes every doubt louder. Stay near if you can.
I cannot see beyond the fire. I hope you can.
Help me sleep without turning every sound into danger.
The guard is real and awake. I am asking you as extra help.
If darkness belongs to you too, keep it quiet tonight.
I cannot sleep, so I may as well test whether you listen.
Punish them for what they did and let everyone see it.
You saw their insult. Show them that you did not approve.
Judge between us, and do not mistake my patience for forgiveness.
I have left punishment to you. Please make it memorable.
I want revenge and keep calling it justice. You know the difference.
Part of me wants you to hurt them. The rest hopes you refuse.
I am too angry to ask for anything decent tonight.
I doubt you listen, which makes this easier to admit. Ruin their day.
If divine justice exists, it could begin with my unpleasant neighbour.
I know this is foolish. I still want you to frighten them.
Teach me to serve without needing everyone to notice.
I have received enough. Show me where I should give.
Keep my faith honest when obedience becomes inconvenient.
Let my actions match the promises I make here.
I keep returning. Perhaps that means more than certainty would.
I want to trust you without pretending my questions disappeared.
Give me enough faith for the next decision, not every decision forever.
I came because habit is cheaper than certainty. Surprise me.
If devotion matters to you, explain why doubt keeps company with mine.
I am kneeling. That is more agreement than you had yesterday.
